correctness.rationale: The final claim is finite Boolean completeness for theoremhood in the unrestricted formula-indexed mu-extension semantics, with at most 2^s carrier elements for a formula with s distinct variable or implication subformulas. Let U contain the non-theorems among these subformulas and T(psi) be the non-theorem conjunctive blocks of psi. The proposed full valuation and full fallback yield U minus T(psi): conjunction uses union of the T sets, and the inclusion test on complements is exactly T(beta) subset T(alpha), the theoremhood test from Lemma 4.4 and Corollary 4.8. Implication therefore gives top on theorems and the prescribed singleton deletion otherwise. Non-theorem roots omit at least one atom; soundness is Theorem 7.2. For the separating formula every two-element evaluation gives top (split on p). The three required failed order tests hold on the stated chain and on its order-embedded copy in the four-element Boolean algebra. Two scientific notes in the frozen text were incorrect: the constructed U for this separator has five elements, so its canonical model is not the claimed tiny model; and the verifier's 576 cases at lines 100–108 concern three-leaf formulas, while the separator checks 32 assignments at lines 109–117. The two corrected complete Markdown files under /workspace/repairs/4 explicitly give the four-element witness and report the tested cases correctly; the proof and checker are unchanged and the verification front matter is preserved. Independent witness replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/4_boundary_witness.py (32 assignments and both refutations). The all-formula result rests on the symbolic induction, not on testing.

value.rationale: This addresses the finite-model question for a specific recently formulated semantics, giving a reusable formula-dependent Boolean countermodel instead of an unrestricted quotient. The small witness explains why validity in all finite Boolean carriers cannot be replaced by testing the two-element one. Neither sharpness of the general bound nor strong completeness for premise sets is claimed.
